name: ShieldTech Enforcer DM-4 'Crossover'
description:
The ShieldTech DM-4 is a dual-mode baton designed for security personnel who require a single tool capable of functioning as both a conventional impact weapon and an electric shock device. In its default impact configuration, it is a 56-centimeter reinforced polycarbonate baton with a weighted polymer core — functionally comparable to a traditional PR-24 in mass and balance, capable of delivering meaningful blunt-force strikes. A recessed toggle switch on the lower grip activates the discharge system, energizing a pair of contact electrodes at the tip and along the upper third of the shaft, allowing the weapon to deliver a 55,000-volt shock on contact during a strike or press application.

The design philosophy addresses a documented problem in security work: the moment of weapon transition. Drawing a separate shock device after establishing impact contact, or vice versa, creates a vulnerability window that has resulted in documented injuries to security personnel. The DM-4 eliminates that window by integrating both functions into a single platform. The electric discharge mode can be activated mid-swing, meaning a strike that makes contact delivers both kinetic and electrical energy simultaneously — a combination ShieldTech's training materials describe as 'synergistic compliance.' Critics have noted that 'synergistic compliance' sounds considerably more benign than 'being hit with a stick that also electrocutes you.'

The DM-4 is certified under MMSS-7 for licensed security use and is a common upgrade purchase for building security firms whose staff already carry the SB-3. It is priced at a point that makes it accessible to most security contractors but slightly out of reach for casual civilian purchase.
legality: Licensed — legal for security contractors with active MMSS-7 credentials; civilian carry requires Tier 2 personal protection permit
specifications: Length: 560mm Weight: 780g Impact Mode: Reinforced polycarbonate, polymer-weighted core Discharge Voltage: 55,000V Amperage: 0.003A Electrode Coverage: Tip + upper 200mm of shaft Mode Switch: Recessed toggle, lower grip Charge Capacity: ~35 full discharges Charge Time: 3.5 hours (inductive) Price: Φ340
tactical_use: Security personnel are trained to use the DM-4 in impact mode for initial distance management and crowd control, transitioning to or combining with discharge mode for close-contact compliance situations. The simultaneous delivery of kinetic and electrical energy during a contact strike significantly increases the probability of immediate subject compliance and is recommended in training for situations where a single-stimulus response has failed. The distributed electrode array along the shaft means that even non-tip strikes can deliver a shock if the discharge mode is active, which requires careful attention to bystander positioning.
cultural_context: The DM-4 is called 'the switch' by security professionals who appreciate its versatility, and 'the crossover' by those on the receiving end of its dual-mode capability. In Tier 2 and 3 entertainment districts where nightclub and venue security carry them openly, the DM-4 has become something of a visual symbol of the mid-tier security professional — more serious than the basic SB-3, not as intimidating as Arcturus hardware, occupying the practical middle ground that most of GLMZ actually lives in.
story_hooks: A series of incidents at a Tier 3 entertainment district involve victims with bruising and electrical burn patterns consistent with DM-4 use — but the venue whose security staff carry DM-4s has airtight camera records showing nothing. Someone is using a DM-4 in the blind spots, and they know exactly where those blind spots are.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian impact baton with a aggressive, purpose-built silhouette. The shaft is straight and cylindrical with a subtle taper toward the tip, featuring a pronounced grip section in the lower third marked by a recessed toggle switch. The upper third shows faint linear scoring along the shaft—the electrode array tracks. Overall impression is corporate-industrial: clean lines, no decorative elements, designed for function rather than intimidation.
physical_description.dimensions: 560mm overall length; 45mm shaft diameter; grip section 120mm with 35mm diameter; tip electrode assembly extends 30mm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced. At 780g, it has substantial presence in the hand without being cumbersome. The weighted polymer core shifts mass toward the tip slightly, creating a natural swing-point that feels controlled rather than wild.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polycarbonate shaft with embedded polymer weighting; aluminum alloy grip frame; surgical-grade stainless steel electrode contacts
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal-black polycarbonate with light surface texturing to reduce glare and improve grip security. The grip section features brushed aluminum with a subtle diamond-knurl pattern. Electrode contacts are polished to a neutral silver-gray. Minimal branding reflects security-sector restraint.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal black primary (polycarbonate shaft), gun-metal gray secondary (grip frame and electrode contacts), with muted blue accent line running 40mm along the lower grip marking the power indicator zone
physical_description.grip_texture: Lower grip is wrapped in a thin layer of rubberized polymer coating with a subtle crosshatch texture—professional, non-slip, designed to shed moisture. Upper shaft is smooth polycarbonate, slightly cool to the touch. The recessed toggle switch has a tactile detent.
distinctive_features: Recessed toggle switch on lower grip with positive mechanical feedback—not a slide, a true toggle requiring deliberate activation
Faint linear electrode scoring visible along upper 200mm of shaft, appearing as thin silver-gray inlays beneath the polycarbonate
Tip assembly: dual-contact electrode configuration—primary strike contact point plus secondary ring electrode 80mm back
Micro-LED charge indicator cluster on grip section (3 small white LEDs showing capacity status)
Inductive charging port recessed into grip base (round magnetic contact plate)
ShieldTech logo stamped in matte silver on grip section
MMSS-7 compliance marking and regulatory text in small font along shaft lower third
Hairline stress-relief grooves around grip-to-shaft junction
Subtle wear pattern on impact tip from training use—micro-scuffing in a radial pattern
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ShieldTech logo (geometric shield with internal crosshatch) stamped at 90-degree angle on grip frame, approximately 40mm from base. Regulatory text (MMSS-7 CERTIFIED / LICENSED USE ONLY) runs vertically along lower shaft in 4pt sans-serif font. Serial number plate (small aluminum rectangle, 20mm x 8mm) affixed to grip base. Model designation 'DM-4' embossed on upper grip.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained field condition. The polycarbonate shows no cracks or serious scarring, but the tip electrode contact exhibits the micro-scuffing pattern expected from regular impact drills and compliance training. Grip rubber shows minor compression wear in the lower contact zone from repeated use. The charging port shows light oxidation from inductive coupling cycles. Scratches are minimal—this is a tool kept in serviceable condition, not display condition.
